The average distance from the Earth to the Sun, which is known as the astronomical unit (AU), is approximately 93 million miles (150 million kilometers).

More specifically:

- The mean (average) distance from the Earth to the Sun is 92,955,807 miles (149,597,870 km).

- This distance varies slightly throughout the year due to the elliptical shape of the Earth's orbit around the Sun. The distance ranges from about 91 million miles (147 million km) at perihelion (closest point) to about 94.5 million miles (152 million km) at aphelion (farthest point).

- This distance is used as a standard unit of measurement for distances within our solar system. For example, the distance from the Earth to Mars can be expressed as around 1.5 AU.

- The time it takes for light to travel from the Earth to the Sun is about 8 minutes and 20 seconds, at the speed of light (approximately 670 million mph or 1.08 billion km/h).

So in summary, the average distance from the Earth to the Sun, the fundamental unit of astronomical measurement, is about 93 million miles or 150 million kilometers.
